rows.t: Antique Bird Print 1772 Buffon Martinet Peru Jay Hand Colored Engraving

det.desc: An original 18th-century hand-colored engraving from Buffon's landmark Histoire Naturelle des Oiseaux, the great French natural history encyclopedia published in Paris from 1771. This plate illustrates the Geai du Pérou — a brilliantly plumed jay from Peru — with Martinet's characteristic precision: a vivid blue face and neck, black throat, emerald green back, and yellow front and tail feathers that leap off the page. She later continued her training at the School of the Art Institute of Chicago, where influential instructors George Bellows and Randall Davey helped shape her modernist direction. Foy began exhibiting in 1922 with the No-Jury Society of Artists and soon gained recognition from the Art Institute of Chicago. rows.t: Pair Vintage Hand Colored Engravings of Bald Eagle and Red Headed Woodpecker

det.desc: Pair Vintage Antique Framed Hand Colored Engravings of Bald Eagle and Red Headed Woodpecker Engraved by W.H. Lizars, Edinburgh. William Home Lizars (1788–1859) was a leading Edinburgh engraver. From 1819 onward he produced plates for a number of natural history works, including Selby's Illustrations of British Ornithology , and his studio engraved and colored the plates for Jardine and Selby's Illustrations of Ornithology (1826–43). The obsolete Latin names match the 1820s–1840s period: Haliaetus leucocephalus for the bald eagle, and Picus erythrocephalus for the red-headed woodpecker, which was later reclassified as Melanerpes . The single birds on plain grounds and the lettering style fit Edinburgh natural-history plates of the 1830s. Edinburgh editions of Alexander Wilson's American Ornithology are the most likely source. SIZE: Both frames are 19.5" H X 16" W These came from my 90 year old mother's house.
